name: Papyrus 52
provenance: Bought in Egypt in 1920 by Bernard Grenfell | Identified and published by C. H. Roberts in 1935
condition: A single damaged leaf fragment, written on both sides
notes: Often called the earliest known fragment of a New Testament text; its date rests on handwriting alone.

name: Codex Alexandrinus
catalog_ids: Gregory–Aland A (02) | Royal MS 1 D V–VIII
contents: Most of the Greek Old Testament (Septuagint) | Most of the New Testament | First Clement | Second Clement (incomplete)
provenance: Given by Cyril Lucaris, Patriarch of Constantinople, to King Charles I in 1627 | Came to the British Museum with the Royal Library in 1757
condition: Incomplete: leaves lost from Matthew, John and 2 Corinthians, and the end of Second Clement
notes: One of the four great uncial codices of the Greek Bible.
